userAgentParser.q1: What information does a User-Agent string contain?
userAgentParser.a1: A User-Agent string provides details regarding the client browser application, rendering engine, operating system platform, CPU architecture, and device form factor.
userAgentParser.q2: Can this parser differentiate human browsers from bots and AI scrapers?
userAgentParser.a2: Yes. The parser maintains signature patterns for search engine bots (Googlebot, Bingbot), social crawlers, and AI scraping agents (OpenAI GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, ByteDance ByteSpider).
userAgentParser.q3: Is my User-Agent string sent to any external server?
userAgentParser.a3: No. The parsing engine executes 100% locally inside your browser memory without sending data to external APIs.
userAgentParser.q4: What does RFC compliant mean for a User-Agent?
userAgentParser.a4: RFC 7231 specifies that HTTP user agents should begin with product identifier tokens (like Mozilla/5.0) and maintain clean token formatting without illegal characters.

base64Encoder.title: Base64 Encoder & Decoder
base64Encoder.subtitle: Encode text to Base64 or decode Base64 strings instantly with absolute client-side privacy.
base64Encoder.aboutText: The Base64 Encoder & Decoder is a high-speed, client-side developer utility that converts plain text, Unicode strings, and binary sequences into standardized RFC 4648 Base64 representations and vice-versa. Operating entirely within browser memory, it guarantees zero network exposure and immediate bi-directional conversion.
base64Encoder.feature1: 100% In-Browser Privacy: All encoding and decoding operations run locally in browser memory without sending data to external servers
base64Encoder.feature2: Full UTF-8 & Unicode Support: Accurately encodes multi-byte Unicode characters, accented letters, and emojis without data loss
base64Encoder.feature3: Bi-Directional Conversion: Seamlessly toggle between Encode (Text to Base64) and Decode (Base64 to Text) modes with automatic live processing
base64Encoder.feature4: Instant Error Handling & Clipboard Copy: Visual validation immediately flags malformed Base64 strings with quick one-click copy
base64Encoder.step1Body: Choose "Encode" to serialize plain text into Base64, or "Decode" to convert a Base64 string back into readable text.
base64Encoder.step2Body: Type or paste your input into the source editor; the tool automatically processes and updates the output in real time.
base64Encoder.step3Body: Review the generated result in the output panel and click "Copy" to copy the result to your clipboard.
base64Encoder.faq1Q: What is Base64 encoding used for?
base64Encoder.faq1A: Base64 is an encoding scheme used to represent binary data in an ASCII string format, commonly used in email headers (MIME), data URLs, and API payloads.
base64Encoder.faq2Q: Does this tool support Unicode and emojis?
base64Encoder.faq2A: Yes, our encoder properly handles UTF-8 byte sequences so emojis, international alphabets, and special symbols are preserved without data corruption.
base64Encoder.faq3Q: Is my data sent to any remote server?
base64Encoder.faq3A: No, never. All calculations are handled locally inside your browser via client-side JavaScript. None of your data is transmitted over the internet or logged on any server.
base64Encoder.faq4Q: Is Base64 the same as encryption?
base64Encoder.faq4A: No. Base64 is an encoding format for data transmission, not an encryption algorithm. It does not provide security or password protection.

jsonFormatter.title: JSON Formatter & Validator
jsonFormatter.subtitle: Format, validate, beautify, and minify JSON payloads instantly in your browser with absolute client-side privacy.
jsonFormatter.aboutText: The JSON Formatter & Validator is an essential client-side utility built for software engineers, API developers, and data architects. It inspects raw or minified JSON strings, highlights structural syntax errors with exact line and column numbers, and formats payloads according to RFC 8259 specifications. All validation happens locally in browser memory without sending data to external APIs.
jsonFormatter.feature1: 100% In-Browser Execution: Safely format private API tokens, user data, and production configs without network exposure
jsonFormatter.feature2: Instant RFC 8259 Syntax Validation: Automatically flags missing commas, trailing delimiters, and unescaped characters with helpful error markers
jsonFormatter.feature3: Bi-Directional Formatting & Minification: Switch between clean 2-space indented readable views and compact single-line minified payloads
jsonFormatter.feature4: One-Click Clipboard Copy: Copy formatted or minified output directly to your system clipboard with instant visual confirmation
jsonFormatter.step1Body: Enter or paste your raw JSON payload into the input editor panel.
jsonFormatter.step2Body: Click "Format / Beautify" to add readable indentation or "Minify" to compress into a compact single-line string.
jsonFormatter.step3Body: Check for syntax validation messages and click "Copy" to use the formatted result in your application.
jsonFormatter.faq1Q: Can this tool format large JSON files?
jsonFormatter.faq1A: Yes, the formatter leverages high-performance JavaScript engine parsers capable of parsing multi-megabyte JSON trees in milliseconds without freezing your browser tab.
jsonFormatter.faq2Q: Is my sensitive JSON data sent to any server?
jsonFormatter.faq2A: No, never. All parsing, validation, beautification, and minification run entirely in client-side memory. Your data never touches any external server or logging facility.
jsonFormatter.faq3Q: What happens when my JSON has a syntax error?
jsonFormatter.faq3A: The validator catches syntax exceptions and displays the exact character position and reason for failure, helping you quickly identify missing quotes, brackets, or commas.
jsonFormatter.faq4Q: Does it support nested arrays and complex objects?
jsonFormatter.faq4A: Yes, it fully supports deeply nested JSON objects, heterogeneous arrays, Unicode strings, boolean values, null values, and arbitrary floating-point numbers per RFC 8259.

ageCalculator.title: Exact Age Calculator
ageCalculator.subtitle: Calculate your precise chronological age in years, months, days, hours, and minutes with upcoming birthday countdown.
ageCalculator.aboutText: The Exact Age Calculator computes your precise chronological age from date of birth down to the minute. Accounting for leap years, variable calendar month lengths, and timezones, it provides a complete chronological breakdown including total days lived, Western zodiac signs, and a countdown to your next birthday.
ageCalculator.feature1: High-Precision Chronological Breakdown: Computes age accurately across leap years, daylight saving boundaries, and calendar variance
ageCalculator.feature2: Multi-Unit Time Metrics: View your lifespan broken down into total months, weeks, days, hours, and minutes lived
ageCalculator.feature3: Next Birthday Countdown & Zodiac: Automatically calculates the remaining days to your next celebration alongside your Western astrological sign
ageCalculator.feature4: One-Click Report Copy: Export a beautifully formatted age and milestone summary to your clipboard with a single click
ageCalculator.step1Body: Choose your day, month, and year of birth from the intuitive date picker.
ageCalculator.step2Body: The tool automatically computes your exact age in years, months, and days with full unit conversions.
ageCalculator.step3Body: Click "Copy Full Report" to save your comprehensive chronological statistics to your clipboard.
ageCalculator.faq1Q: How does this calculator account for leap years?
ageCalculator.faq1A: The algorithm computes elapsed leap days dynamically by checking Gregorian calendar intercalary rules (years divisible by 4, except centuries not divisible by 400), ensuring exact day counts.
ageCalculator.faq2Q: Can I calculate the age of an event or historical milestone?
ageCalculator.faq2A: Yes, you can enter any past date to find the exact elapsed time between that milestone and today's date.
ageCalculator.faq3Q: Is my birthdate recorded or stored?
ageCalculator.faq3A: No. All date arithmetic occurs 100% locally in your browser. No birthdates or personal identifiers are stored, tracked, or sent across the internet.
ageCalculator.faq4Q: Why do total days differ from simply multiplying years by 365?
ageCalculator.faq4A: A solar year contains approximately 365.2422 days. Counting exact calendar months and leap years accounts for the extra days that simple multiplication ignores.

caseConverter.title: Text Case Converter
caseConverter.subtitle: Transform text between camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, UPPERCASE, lowercase, Title Case, and PascalCase.

caseConverter.aboutText: The Text Case Converter is a comprehensive text manipulation utility designed for programmers, content creators, and copywriters. It rapidly converts strings between standard programming naming conventions (camelCase, snake_case, kebab-case, PascalCase, CONSTANT_CASE) and typographical formats (Title Case, Sentence case, Alternating case). All conversions run instantly in client-side memory.
caseConverter.feature1: 12+ Essential Case Formats: Convert strings effortlessly between developer naming conventions and editorial casing
caseConverter.feature2: Special Character & Delimiter Preservation: Intelligently handles spaces, underscores, hyphens, and multi-word token boundaries
caseConverter.feature3: Real-Time Statistics: Displays live character, word, sentence, and line count metrics alongside converted results
caseConverter.feature4: Instant Copy & Clear: One-click actions to copy formatted strings directly to your clipboard or clear workspace
caseConverter.step1Body: Type or paste your text into the input workspace.

caseConverter.step3Body: Review the converted result and click the "Copy" button to copy it to your clipboard.
caseConverter.faq1Q: What is the difference between camelCase and PascalCase?
caseConverter.faq1A: In camelCase, the first letter is lowercase and subsequent words start with an uppercase letter (myVariableName). In PascalCase, every word starts with an uppercase letter (MyClassName).
caseConverter.faq2Q: How does Title Case handle minor words like "and", "the", and "in"?
caseConverter.faq2A: Our Title Case converter adheres to standard English capitalization guidelines, capitalizing major words while keeping articles, short conjunctions, and prepositions lowercase unless they start the sentence.
caseConverter.faq3Q: Is my input text stored or monitored?
caseConverter.faq3A: No. All text manipulations run exclusively in your browser via client-side JavaScript. No text is recorded, analyzed, or sent to external servers.
caseConverter.faq4Q: Can this tool handle programming code snippets?
caseConverter.faq4A: Yes, it is specifically optimized for variable renaming, identifier normalization, and database column naming transformations.

checksumCalculator.title: File & Text Checksum Calculator
checksumCalculator.subtitle: Generate MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 cryptographic checksums to verify data integrity.
checksumCalculator.inputPlaceholder: Type or paste your text here...
checksumCalculator.aboutText: The File & Text Checksum Calculator is an in-browser cryptographic hashing utility designed to verify data integrity and detect file tampering. Using the browser's native Web Crypto API, it computes MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 cryptographic digests for strings and binary files. Processing is executed completely locally on your hardware without server uploads.
checksumCalculator.feature1: Native Web Crypto API Acceleration: Generates SHA-256 and SHA-512 hashes using hardware-accelerated browser primitives
checksumCalculator.feature2: Dual Text and File Support: Calculate cryptographic digests for raw text strings or directly inspect local files
checksumCalculator.feature3: Multi-Algorithm Comparison: Simultaneously inspect MD5, SHA-1, SHA-256, and SHA-512 digests for comprehensive verification
checksumCalculator.feature4: Integrity Verification Matcher: Compare computed checksums against vendor-provided hashes with instant visual pass/fail indicators
checksumCalculator.step1Body: Choose between hashing raw text or uploading a file from your computer.
checksumCalculator.step2Body: Choose your desired hashing standard (SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1, or MD5).
checksumCalculator.step3Body: Compare the resulting hash against your reference checksum or click "Copy" to copy the hexadecimal digest.
checksumCalculator.faq1Q: What is a cryptographic checksum used for?
checksumCalculator.faq1A: A checksum acts as a unique digital fingerprint for data. Developers and system administrators use checksums to verify that downloaded software, ISO images, or packages have not been corrupted or tampered with.
checksumCalculator.faq2Q: Are my files uploaded over the internet?
checksumCalculator.faq2A: No, never. The file checksum is calculated locally using the browser's FileReader and Web Crypto APIs. Your file never leaves your computer.
checksumCalculator.faq3Q: Which hash algorithm is recommended for security?
checksumCalculator.faq3A: SHA-256 or SHA-512 are strongly recommended for security verification. Legacy algorithms like MD5 and SHA-1 are cryptographically broken and should only be used for non-security data integrity checks.
checksumCalculator.faq4Q: Can I calculate checksums for large files?
checksumCalculator.faq4A: Yes, the tool reads files in memory chunks via web streams, enabling checksum generation for large installers and disk images without crashing your browser.

colorConverter.aboutText: The Color Converter & Palette Inspector is an indispensable tool for UI/UX designers, CSS developers, and graphic artists. It converts color values across HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, and CMYK formats, computes complementary palettes, and calculates WCAG 2.1 accessibility contrast ratios against light and dark backgrounds in real time.
colorConverter.feature1: Multi-Format Color Translation: Instantly converts between HEX, RGB, RGBA, HSL, HSLA, HSV, and print-ready CMYK values
colorConverter.feature2: Interactive Color Picker & Sliders: Fine-tune hues, saturation, and luminance with an interactive visual picker
colorConverter.feature3: WCAG 2.1 Contrast Ratio Analysis: Real-time readability ratings for text on white and dark backgrounds to meet accessibility standards
colorConverter.feature4: Complementary Harmony Generation: Automatically discovers monochromatic, analogous, and complementary color variations
colorConverter.step1Body: Type any HEX code (e.g., #3B82F6), RGB string, or select a hue using the visual color wheel.
colorConverter.step2Body: View synchronized representations across HEX, RGB, HSL, HSV, and CMYK formats simultaneously.
colorConverter.step3Body: Click the copy icon beside any color format to copy CSS-ready values directly to your clipboard.
colorConverter.faq1Q: What is the difference between RGB and CMYK?
colorConverter.faq1A: RGB (Red, Green, Blue) is an additive color model designed for digital screens that emit light. CMYK (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, Black) is a subtractive color model designed for physical ink printing on paper.
colorConverter.faq2Q: Why is HSL favored by modern CSS developers?
colorConverter.faq2A: HSL (Hue, Saturation, Lightness) aligns with human perception, making it intuitive to adjust brightness, create hover states, or build theme palettes by varying lightness while keeping hue constant.
colorConverter.faq3Q: How does WCAG contrast ratio score work?
colorConverter.faq3A: WCAG 2.1 requires a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text (AA level) and 7:1 for enhanced accessibility (AAA level). Our tool calculates these ratios dynamically to ensure readability.
colorConverter.faq4A: Yes, the converter supports 8-digit HEX codes (HEX8) as well as RGBA and HSLA strings with variable opacity percentages.

compoundInterestCalculator.title: Compound Interest Calculator
compoundInterestCalculator.subtitle: Project investment growth over time with customizable principal, annual rate, compounding frequencies, and monthly contributions.
compoundInterestCalculator.aboutText: The Compound Interest Calculator is a financial modeling utility designed to forecast wealth accumulation, retirement savings, and investment returns over time. Using the standard compound interest formula with periodic contributions, it models portfolio growth across annual, semi-annual, quarterly, monthly, or daily compounding intervals.
compoundInterestCalculator.feature1: Customizable Compounding Frequencies: Calculate growth compounded daily, monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually
compoundInterestCalculator.feature2: Regular Contribution Modeling: Factor in ongoing monthly or annual deposits to visualize dollar-cost averaging growth
compoundInterestCalculator.feature3: Detailed Year-by-Year Breakdown: Inspect exact interest accrued versus principal contributed across each investment year
compoundInterestCalculator.feature4: 100% Client-Side Privacy: Your financial figures, net worth goals, and savings plans remain entirely private on your device
compoundInterestCalculator.step1Body: Specify your starting investment balance and anticipated annual interest rate.
compoundInterestCalculator.step2Body: Define the investment term in years and specify recurring monthly or annual contribution amounts.
compoundInterestCalculator.step3Body: Examine total future balance, total interest earned, and annual growth trajectories.
compoundInterestCalculator.faq1A: Compound interest is interest calculated on the initial principal plus all previously accumulated interest from past periods, allowing wealth to grow exponentially over time.
compoundInterestCalculator.faq2Q: How does compounding frequency impact returns?
compoundInterestCalculator.faq2A: More frequent compounding intervals (such as daily or monthly versus annually) generate slightly higher returns because interest begins generating its own interest sooner.
compoundInterestCalculator.faq3A: The Rule of 72 is a quick estimation formula: divide 72 by your annual interest rate to determine approximately how many years it will take to double your investment.
compoundInterestCalculator.faq4Q: Does this calculator account for inflation or taxes?
compoundInterestCalculator.faq4A: This calculator displays nominal investment returns. To estimate real returns after inflation, you can subtract your estimated inflation rate (e.g., 2-3%) from your expected interest rate.

cronExpressionGenerator.title: Cron Expression Generator & Parser
cronExpressionGenerator.subtitle: Build, decode, and schedule standard 5-part and 6-part cron expressions with human-readable explanations.
cronExpressionGenerator.aboutText: The Cron Expression Generator & Parser is an essential DevOps and backend engineering utility that translates between human-readable scheduling rules and standard POSIX cron syntax. Supporting standard 5-field crontabs (minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week) and 6-field quartz syntax, it explains schedules in plain English and calculates upcoming trigger times.
cronExpressionGenerator.feature1: Visual Schedule Builder: Build complex recurring schedules using intuitive dropdowns and selectors without memorizing syntax
cronExpressionGenerator.feature2: Human-Readable Schedule Translation: Instantly translates cryptic cron strings (like "*/15 0-6 * * 1-5") into clear English descriptions
cronExpressionGenerator.feature3: Upcoming Execution Timestamps: Calculates and previews the next scheduled run times to prevent scheduling mistakes
cronExpressionGenerator.feature4: Universal Platform Compatibility: Generates expressions compatible with Linux crontab, GitHub Actions, AWS EventBridge, and Kubernetes CronJobs
cronExpressionGenerator.step1Body: Choose recurrence intervals for minutes, hours, days of the month, months, and days of the week.
cronExpressionGenerator.step2Body: Review the generated cron expression alongside its natural-language translation and upcoming execution preview.
cronExpressionGenerator.step3Body: Click "Copy" to paste the validated cron string directly into your crontab, CI/CD pipeline, or infrastructure code.
cronExpressionGenerator.faq1Q: What do the 5 fields in a standard cron expression represent?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq1A: From left to right: Minute (0-59), Hour (0-23), Day of Month (1-31), Month (1-12 or JAN-DEC), and Day of Week (0-6 or SUN-SAT, where 0 and 7 are Sunday).
cronExpressionGenerator.faq2Q: What does the asterisk (*) and slash (/) mean in cron?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq2A: An asterisk (*) means "every value" (e.g., every minute). A slash (/) specifies step increments (e.g., */5 in the minute field means "every 5 minutes").
cronExpressionGenerator.faq3Q: Can this expression be used in GitHub Actions?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq3A: Yes! GitHub Actions workflow triggers use standard POSIX cron expressions on the UTC timezone schedule.
cronExpressionGenerator.faq4Q: How do I specify run times only on weekdays?
cronExpressionGenerator.faq4A: Set the Day of Week field to "1-5" (Monday through Friday). For example, "0 9 * * 1-5" runs at 9:00 AM every Monday through Friday.

cspHeaderBuilder.title: CSP Header Builder & Validator
cspHeaderBuilder.subtitle: Construct, test, and validate Content-Security-Policy HTTP headers to protect web apps from XSS and data injection.
cspHeaderBuilder.aboutText: The CSP Header Builder & Validator is a web application security utility designed to construct, evaluate, and test Content-Security-Policy (CSP Level 3) response headers. By defining granular directives for scripts, styles, images, iframes, and connect endpoints, it helps developers prevent cross-site scripting (XSS), clickjacking, and unauthorized data exfiltration.
cspHeaderBuilder.feature1: Comprehensive Directive Coverage: Configure default-src, script-src, style-src, img-src, connect-src, frame-ancestors, and object-src
cspHeaderBuilder.feature2: Security Risk Analysis: Automatically flags dangerous directives like "unsafe-inline" and "unsafe-eval" with hardening recommendations
cspHeaderBuilder.feature3: Nginx, Apache, & Meta Export: Generates ready-to-paste snippets for Nginx configs, Apache .htaccess, and HTML meta tags
cspHeaderBuilder.feature4: Client-Side Policy Testing: Validate existing CSP headers without transmitting sensitive server configurations across the web
cspHeaderBuilder.step1Body: Set trust origins and source domains for scripts, stylesheets, media assets, and API connections.
cspHeaderBuilder.step2Body: Check the automated risk validator to ensure your policy does not permit permissive wildcards or dangerous execution keywords.
cspHeaderBuilder.step3Body: Export the formatted Content-Security-Policy header for Nginx, Apache, or HTML meta tags with one click.
cspHeaderBuilder.faq1Q: What is a Content Security Policy (CSP)?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq1A: CSP is an HTTP response header that instructs modern web browsers which resources (scripts, images, stylesheets) are permitted to load and execute, mitigating XSS attacks.
cspHeaderBuilder.faq2Q: Why should I avoid "unsafe-inline" in script-src?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq2A: Allowing "unsafe-inline" lets attackers execute injected inline scripts via reflected or stored XSS vulnerabilities. Use cryptographic nonces or hashes instead.
cspHeaderBuilder.faq3Q: What is the difference between CSP and CORS?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq3A: CSP controls which origins a browser page can load resources from. CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) governs whether an external origin can read resources from your server API.
cspHeaderBuilder.faq4Q: Can I test CSP in Report-Only mode?
cspHeaderBuilder.faq4A: Yes. You can use the "Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only" header to monitor violations sent to a reporting endpoint without blocking resource execution.

csvToJson.title: CSV to JSON Converter
csvToJson.subtitle: Convert CSV and TSV spreadsheets into structured JSON arrays and objects with automatic delimiter detection.
csvToJson.aboutText: The CSV to JSON Converter is a client-side data transformation utility built for software developers, data scientists, and analysts. It parses comma-separated (CSV), tab-separated (TSV), and custom delimited tabular files into formatted JSON arrays of objects. Operating entirely in browser memory, it handles multi-megabyte datasets with high performance.
csvToJson.feature1: Auto-Delimiter Detection: Automatically identifies commas, semicolons, tabs, and pipes to parse tables without manual configuration
csvToJson.feature2: Type Inference & Parsing: Automatically casts numeric values, booleans, and null fields to native JSON types instead of strings
csvToJson.feature3: Dual Output Modes: Choose between an Array of Objects (keyed by header row) or a 2D Array of Rows for compact payloads
csvToJson.feature4: 100% In-Browser Privacy: Your sensitive financial spreadsheets and customer records never leave your local device
csvToJson.step1Body: Paste your raw CSV text into the editor or upload a .csv or .tsv file from your device.
csvToJson.step2Body: Toggle type inference, select header parsing, and choose between formatted or minified JSON.
csvToJson.step3Body: Inspect the generated JSON tree and click "Copy" or "Download" to save the file.
csvToJson.faq1Q: Does this tool handle commas inside quoted values?
csvToJson.faq1A: Yes, the parser adheres to RFC 4180 specifications, correctly handling escaped quotes, commas inside text fields, and multi-line cells.
csvToJson.faq2Q: Is my CSV file data uploaded to any server?
csvToJson.faq2A: No, never. All parsing and conversion are executed locally in your browser memory via JavaScript. No data is stored, transmitted, or logged.
csvToJson.faq3Q: Can I convert TSV (Tab-Separated Values) or semicolon-delimited files?
csvToJson.faq3A: Yes, our automatic delimiter detection identifies tabs, semicolons, pipes (|), and commas automatically.
csvToJson.faq4Q: What is the maximum file size I can convert?
csvToJson.faq4A: Because processing occurs locally in memory, you can convert multi-megabyte CSV files containing tens of thousands of rows without server timeout errors.

curlToFetch.title: cURL to Fetch & Axios Converter
curlToFetch.subtitle: Translate cURL commands into idiomatic JavaScript fetch() and Axios HTTP requests instantly.
curlToFetch.aboutText: The cURL to Fetch & Axios Converter is a browser-based developer utility that deconstructs raw cURL terminal commands and translates them into modern, production-ready JavaScript code. It parses HTTP methods (-X, --request), headers (-H), basic and bearer authentication (-u, --user), query parameters, URL-encoded forms, and JSON payloads (--data, -d, --data-raw). The tool outputs clean Fetch API promises using async/await and Axios request configurations ready for frontend or Node.js applications.
curlToFetch.feature1: Comprehensive cURL Syntax Parsing: Accurately handles headers, query params, cookies, basic auth, and multipart form-data
curlToFetch.feature2: Dual Modern Output Formats: Instantly toggle between browser-native Fetch API (async/await) and Axios client syntax
curlToFetch.feature3: Zero Server Transmission: Command parsing and code generation execute entirely in browser memory for complete credential safety
curlToFetch.feature4: Production-Ready Formatting: Generates clean, properly indented, error-handled JavaScript snippets with one-click copy
curlToFetch.step1Body: Copy a cURL command from your terminal, API documentation, or browser DevTools Network tab and paste it into the editor.
curlToFetch.step2Body: Switch between native browser Fetch and Axios tabs to compare syntax and request structure.
curlToFetch.step3Body: Review the formatted JavaScript code, then click "Copy" to import the request snippet directly into your codebase.
curlToFetch.faq1Q: Which cURL flags and options are supported?
curlToFetch.faq1A: The parser handles primary HTTP flags including -X/--request (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH), -H/--header, -d/--data/--data-raw (JSON and form data), -u/--user (Basic Auth), and URL parameters.
curlToFetch.faq2Q: Does this converter upload sensitive API tokens or passwords?
curlToFetch.faq2A: No. The entire conversion logic executes client-side in your browser using pure JavaScript parsing. No commands or authorization headers are sent to remote servers.
curlToFetch.faq3Q: Does the generated Fetch code support error handling?
curlToFetch.faq3A: Yes, generated Fetch examples demonstrate standard HTTP response status validation (res.ok) and asynchronous JSON body resolution.
curlToFetch.faq4Q: Can I convert commands exported from Chrome or Firefox DevTools?
curlToFetch.faq4A: Yes. Right-click any network request in Chrome, Firefox, or Safari, select "Copy as cURL", and paste it directly into this tool.

curlToPython.subtitle: Transform cURL terminal commands into idiomatic Python requests code instantly with zero latency.

It intelligently parses HTTP request methods, custom headers, cookies, URL parameters, basic authentication credentials, and data payloads (both application/json and form-encoded data). curlToPython.feature1: Idiomatic Python Output: Formats payloads as Python dictionaries, preserving types, nested keys, and custom headers
curlToPython.feature2: Smart Auth & Payload Detection: Automatically maps -u flags to requests.auth.HTTPBasicAuth and JSON payloads to json=
curlToPython.feature3: 100% In-Browser Privacy: API keys, bearer tokens, and confidential request bodies never leave your local browser environment
curlToPython.feature4: Instant Syntax Highlighting: Clean Python code structure formatted according to PEP 8 standards with rapid copy support

curlToPython.step3Body: Click "Copy Code" to paste the snippet into your Jupyter notebook, FastAPI service, or automation script.
curlToPython.faq1Q: Does this tool use Python requests or httpx?
curlToPython.faq1A: It generates standard Python requests code with clean dictionaries for headers, params, and JSON data. The resulting syntax is easily adaptable to httpx as well.
curlToPython.faq2Q: How are JSON bodies formatted in Python?
curlToPython.faq2A: If the cURL command contains valid JSON data in -d or --data-raw, it is converted into a native Python dictionary passed to the json= parameter.
curlToPython.faq3Q: Are sensitive authorization headers leaked during conversion?
curlToPython.faq3A: Never. All tokenization, parsing, and code synthesis take place exclusively in client-side memory without network transmissions.
curlToPython.faq4Q: How does it handle multiline cURL commands?
curlToPython.faq4A: The parser automatically strips backslash line continuations (\) and normalizes whitespace before analyzing flags and arguments.

discountCalculator.title: Discount & Sale Price Calculator
discountCalculator.subtitle: Calculate retail sale prices, customer savings, stacked percentage discounts, and original pre-sale prices.
discountCalculator.aboutText: The Discount & Sale Price Calculator is an indispensable retail and financial planning tool designed to compute exact savings, post-discount prices, and multi-tier stacked discounts. It supports three distinct modes: finding the sale price given a discount percentage, reverse-engineering the original price from a discounted price tag, and calculating stacked promotional discounts (e.g., 20% off plus an extra 15% clearance). All calculations display effective net savings without rounding discrepancies.
discountCalculator.feature1: Three Calculation Modes: Calculate sale price, reverse-engineer original price, or evaluate stacked discounts
discountCalculator.feature2: Accurate Multi-Tier Stacking: Correctly calculates sequential discounts applied to reduced balances rather than misleading simple sums
discountCalculator.feature3: Dynamic Real-Time Breakdown: Instantly view monetary amount saved, final customer payable amount, and effective discount rate
discountCalculator.feature4: International Currency Formatting: Seamlessly adapts currency symbols and numeric separators according to the active locale
discountCalculator.step1Body: Choose "Find Sale Price", "Find Original Price", or "Stacked Discounts" depending on your retail scenario.
discountCalculator.step2Body: Input the original amount, discounted price, or sequential discount percentages.
discountCalculator.step3Body: Inspect your total monetary savings and effective percentage, then click "Copy Breakdown".
discountCalculator.faq1Q: How do stacked discounts actually work?
discountCalculator.faq1A: Stacked discounts are applied sequentially. For example, a 20% discount followed by an additional 10% discount results in an effective 28% total discount, not 30%, because the second discount applies to the already discounted price.
discountCalculator.faq2Q: Can I find the original price if I only know what I paid?
discountCalculator.faq2A: Yes. Switch to "Find Original Price", enter the final amount paid and the discount rate applied, and the tool will calculate the pre-discount sticker price.
discountCalculator.faq3Q: Does this calculator support decimals and tax?
discountCalculator.faq3A: Yes, you can enter fractional currency values (e.g. 19.99). You can also apply tax percentages by compounding or adjusting the baseline price.
discountCalculator.faq4Q: Is any financial data stored or uploaded?
discountCalculator.faq4A: No. All calculations are executed locally in your browser session and are never logged or transmitted.

gradeCalculator.aboutText: The Weighted Grade & Final Exam Calculator enables students, educators, and academic advisors to determine accurate cumulative course grades based on weighted syllabus categories. With support for assignments, midterms, quizzes, and projects, the tool computes weighted percentage averages, standard letter grade equivalents, and 4.0 scale GPA conversions. Its built-in "What-If" final exam calculator reveals the exact score needed on remaining coursework to secure a desired target grade.
gradeCalculator.feature1: Flexible Weighted Categories: Add unlimited assignments, homework, labs, and exams with individual percentage weights
gradeCalculator.feature2: What-If Final Exam Projection: Automatically calculates the exact exam grade required to earn an A, B, or custom target percentage
gradeCalculator.feature3: Letter Grade & GPA Mapping: Automatically converts numerical averages into standard academic letter grades and 4.0 scale GPA
gradeCalculator.feature4: Validation & Summary Export: Visual validation flags when total category weight exceeds 100%, with easy one-click summary copying

gradeCalculator.faq1A: In a weighted grading system, each assignment category contributes a fixed percentage to your final course grade. Each category's percentage score is multiplied by its weight, and the products are summed.
gradeCalculator.faq2Q: What happens if total weight does not equal 100%?
gradeCalculator.faq2A: The calculator displays your current standing based on the weights completed so far, and shows the remaining percentage allocated to upcoming exams.
gradeCalculator.faq3Q: How does the What-If calculator determine my needed exam score?
gradeCalculator.faq3A: It uses the formula: Needed Score = (Desired Grade - Current Weighted Points) / Remaining Weight, identifying whether your goal is realistic or mathematically impossible.
gradeCalculator.faq4Q: Are my grades stored on any server?

hashGenerator.title: Cryptographic Hash Generator (SHA-256, SHA-512, MD5)
hashGenerator.subtitle: Generate SHA-256, SHA-512, and MD5 cryptographic hashes instantly with client-side security.
hashGenerator.aboutText: The Cryptographic Hash Generator is a high-performance, browser-based security utility for producing deterministic, one-way hash digests from arbitrary text or binary data. Supporting standard cryptographic hashing algorithms—including SHA-256, SHA-512, and legacy MD5—the tool operates directly within browser memory. It is widely used by cybersecurity engineers, developers, and system administrators for file integrity validation, password hashing analysis, and digital signature verification.
hashGenerator.feature1: Multi-Algorithm Simultaneous Hashing: Computes SHA-256, SHA-512, and MD5 digests concurrently in real time as you type
hashGenerator.feature2: 100% Client-Side Cryptography: Operates completely offline in local memory without transmitting sensitive text to external servers
hashGenerator.feature3: Cryptographic Standard Compliance: Adheres strictly to NIST FIPS 180-4 (SHA family) and RFC 1321 (MD5) specifications
hashGenerator.feature4: One-Click Hash Export: Clean hexadecimal lowercase digests with convenient one-click copy buttons for rapid clipboard transfer
hashGenerator.step1Body: Type or paste your secret string, token, or data payload into the input editor.
hashGenerator.step2Body: Review the computed hexadecimal hash digests across MD5 (128-bit), SHA-256 (256-bit), and SHA-512 (512-bit).
hashGenerator.step3Body: Click "Copy" next to the target hash algorithm to save the digest string to your clipboard.
hashGenerator.faq1Q: Can a cryptographic hash be decrypted back to the original text?
hashGenerator.faq1A: No. Cryptographic hashes are one-way mathematical functions. You cannot reverse or decrypt a hash digest back into plaintext; you can only verify matches by hashing candidate inputs.
hashGenerator.faq2Q: What is the difference between SHA-256 and MD5?
hashGenerator.faq2A: MD5 produces a 128-bit digest and is cryptographically broken due to known collision vulnerabilities, used primarily for legacy checksums. SHA-256 produces a collision-resistant 256-bit digest recommended for modern security standards.
hashGenerator.faq3Q: Is this hash generator safe for sensitive passwords and API keys?
hashGenerator.faq3A: Yes. All hashing algorithms run 100% client-side inside your browser engine. Zero input characters or hashes are ever sent over the internet.
hashGenerator.faq4Q: Does case sensitivity affect the generated hash?
hashGenerator.faq4A: Yes. Cryptographic hash functions exhibit the avalanche effect: even changing a single character or its case produces a completely different hash digest.

hmacGenerator.title: HMAC Signature Generator
hmacGenerator.subtitle: Generate secure Hash-based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA512, HMAC-MD5) instantly.
hmacGenerator.aboutText: The HMAC Signature Generator is a specialized cryptographic utility designed to compute Hash-based Message Authentication Codes (HMAC) compliant with RFC 2104 and FIPS PUB 198. By combining a shared secret cryptographic key with a message payload through an underlying hash function (SHA-256, SHA-512, or MD5), HMAC guarantees both data integrity and authenticity. It is essential for signing REST API requests (e.g., AWS Signature Version 4, Stripe webhooks, GitHub webhooks) and verifying message authenticity.
hmacGenerator.feature1: Standard Algorithm Selection: Supports HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA512, and HMAC-MD5 with exact cryptographic adherence
hmacGenerator.feature2: Client-Side Key Isolation: Shared secret keys and private messages are processed strictly in browser memory, never sent over the network
hmacGenerator.feature3: Real-Time Live Calculation: Automatically recalculates signatures immediately upon modifying either the key, message, or algorithm
hmacGenerator.feature4: Hexadecimal Digest Formatting: Produces standardized lowercase hexadecimal signature strings ready for HTTP header authorization
hmacGenerator.step1Body: Input your shared secret key or API signing secret into the designated key field.
hmacGenerator.step2Body: Choose HMAC-SHA256, SHA-512, or MD5, and paste your JSON payload or request string.
hmacGenerator.step3Body: Review the resulting hexadecimal HMAC signature and click "Copy" to use in your API headers.
hmacGenerator.faq1Q: What is an HMAC and how does it differ from a regular hash?
hmacGenerator.faq1A: A standard hash (like SHA-256) only verifies data integrity. An HMAC incorporates a secret cryptographic key, ensuring both data integrity and proof that the message originated from a party holding the secret key.
hmacGenerator.faq2Q: Is my secret key safe when using this tool?
hmacGenerator.faq2A: Yes, completely. All cryptographic operations are executed locally in your browser using client-side JavaScript. Your secret key and message payload are never transmitted to any external server.
hmacGenerator.faq3Q: Which HMAC algorithm should I choose for modern webhooks?
hmacGenerator.faq3A: HMAC-SHA256 is the industry standard for modern webhooks (used by GitHub, Stripe, Shopify, and Slack) offering high performance and robust security.
hmacGenerator.faq4Q: Can HMAC signatures prevent replay attacks?
hmacGenerator.faq4A: HMAC itself verifies message authenticity. To prevent replay attacks, webhooks commonly include a timestamp in the signed payload and verify it against a short validity window.

htmlEncoderDecoder.title: HTML Entity Encoder & Decoder
htmlEncoderDecoder.subtitle: Convert special characters into HTML entities or decode entities back to plaintext instantly.
htmlEncoderDecoder.aboutText: The HTML Entity Encoder & Decoder is a developer utility that converts reserved characters, symbols, and Unicode glyphs into standardized HTML entities (e.g., <, >, &) and decodes encoded markup back into readable text. Essential for preventing Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities, displaying raw code snippets inside HTML documents, and debugging encoded web content, this tool processes text in real time entirely within your browser.
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature1: Bi-Directional Conversion: Seamlessly toggle between Encode (Text to HTML Entities) and Decode (Entities to Plaintext)
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature2: Comprehensive Character Mapping: Safely encodes reserved characters (<, >, &, ", ') as well as high-order Unicode symbols
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature3: XSS Mitigation Support: Prepares user input strings for safe inclusion within HTML markup and templates
htmlEncoderDecoder.feature4: Zero Server Processing: All string parsing and entity conversions execute client-side for maximum speed and data privacy
htmlEncoderDecoder.step1Body: Choose "Encode" to convert special characters into entities, or "Decode" to restore entities to text.
htmlEncoderDecoder.step2Body: Paste your HTML snippet, code block, or entity-encoded string into the input panel.
htmlEncoderDecoder.step3Body: Review the converted output in the preview panel and click "Copy" to save to your clipboard.
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq1Q: Why is HTML entity encoding important?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq1A: In HTML, characters like <, >, and & have structural syntactic meaning. If untrusted input containing these characters is inserted directly into a page without encoding, browsers may execute malicious scripts, resulting in XSS vulnerabilities.
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq2Q: What are the most common HTML entities?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq2A: The five core XML/HTML entities are: < (<), > (>), & (&), " ("), and ' (').
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq3Q: Does this tool decode named entities as well as numeric entities?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq3A: Yes. It decodes named entities (such as © and  ) as well as decimal (©) and hexadecimal (©) numeric character references.
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq4Q: Is my HTML data sent to a backend server?
htmlEncoderDecoder.faq4A: No. All encoding and decoding operations take place in your browser memory using native DOM parser APIs, ensuring complete confidentiality.

httpHeaderInspector.title: HTTP Header Inspector & Parser
httpHeaderInspector.subtitle: Deconstruct raw HTTP request or response headers into structured key-value maps with security analysis.
httpHeaderInspector.aboutText: The HTTP Header Inspector & Parser is an essential networking and web security tool that parses raw HTTP request and response headers into clear, structured key-value tables. It automatically identifies core networking parameters (Host, User-Agent, Content-Type, Accept-Encoding), detects caching directives (Cache-Control, ETag, Age), and highlights critical security headers (Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options). Perfect for debugging API responses and validating web server security configurations.
httpHeaderInspector.feature1: Instant Raw Header Parsing: Automatically strips status lines and tokenizes multiline headers into structured key-value pairs
httpHeaderInspector.feature2: Security Header Identification: Highlights presence and values of vital defense-in-depth headers like CSP, HSTS, and CORS
httpHeaderInspector.feature3: Clean JSON & Table Export: Formats parsed headers into accessible tables with single-click JSON clipboard export
httpHeaderInspector.feature4: 100% Private Client Analysis: No network requests are made; analysis occurs entirely in browser memory on pasted text
httpHeaderInspector.step1Body: Copy raw response headers from curl, Postman, or your browser DevTools Network tab and paste them in.
httpHeaderInspector.step2Body: Review the parsed headers categorized by standard protocol, caching, and security attributes.
httpHeaderInspector.step3Body: Click "Copy" to export the parsed header object as formatted JSON for use in automated tests or reports.
httpHeaderInspector.faq1Q: What headers are most critical for web application security?
httpHeaderInspector.faq1A: Key security headers include Content-Security-Policy (CSP) to mitigate XSS, Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) to enforce HTTPS, X-Frame-Options to block clickjacking, and X-Content-Type-Options to prevent MIME-sniffing.
httpHeaderInspector.faq2Q: Can I parse both HTTP request and response headers?
httpHeaderInspector.faq2A: Yes. The parser recognizes both request headers (e.g., Authorization, Cookie, Accept) and response headers (e.g., Set-Cookie, Cache-Control, Server).
httpHeaderInspector.faq3Q: How does it handle duplicate headers?
httpHeaderInspector.faq3A: Per RFC 7230, headers with duplicate field names (such as Set-Cookie or Accept) are properly preserved and grouped rather than overwritten.
httpHeaderInspector.faq4Q: Does this tool inspect headers over live network connections?
httpHeaderInspector.faq4A: This tool is an offline parser designed for analyzing pasted header blocks without sending outbound HTTP probes, ensuring maximum security and zero firewall restrictions.

imageResizer.faq1Q: Does resizing reduce image visual quality?
imageResizer.faq1A: Downscaling preserves crisp details using browser bicubic smoothing. Upscaling beyond original dimensions naturally has diminishing returns as missing pixels must be interpolated.
imageResizer.faq2Q: Are my photos uploaded to any external server?

imageResizer.faq3Q: What image file formats are supported?

imageResizer.faq4Q: Is there a file size limit for resizing?
imageResizer.faq4A: There are no arbitrary server upload limits. The only constraint is your device's available RAM to hold the canvas bitmap in memory.

It correctly resolves primitive data types (string, int64, float64, bool), infers nested struct models, handles slices and arrays, accommodates nullable values with pointers or interface{}, and generates canonical struct tags (`json:"key_name"`). Designed for rapid API development and microservice modeling.
jsonToGoStruct.feature1: Idiomatic Go Naming: Converts snake_case and camelCase JSON keys into exported PascalCase Go struct field names
jsonToGoStruct.feature2: Automatic Type Inference: Accurately differentiates integers, floating-point numbers, booleans, strings, and slice types
jsonToGoStruct.feature3: Nested Struct Extraction: Decomposes deeply nested JSON objects into modular, reusable sub-struct definitions
jsonToGoStruct.feature4: Private In-Browser Generation: Generates Go source code in browser memory without transmitting API payloads over the network

jsonToGoStruct.faq1Q: How are nested JSON objects handled?
jsonToGoStruct.faq1A: The generator creates independent, named Go sub-structs for nested JSON objects, ensuring clean, modular, and readable Go code.
jsonToGoStruct.faq2Q: Does it handle null values and empty arrays?
jsonToGoStruct.faq2A: Yes. Nullable properties are typed safely using pointers or interface{} to prevent JSON unmarshaling panics.
jsonToGoStruct.faq3Q: Are json struct tags automatically added?
jsonToGoStruct.faq3A: Yes. Every struct field includes the standard `json:"key"` tag matching the exact casing of the original JSON key.
jsonToGoStruct.faq4Q: Is my proprietary JSON schema uploaded to any server?
jsonToGoStruct.faq4A: No. All parsing, type inference, and Go code synthesis occur strictly in client-side JavaScript within your browser.

Supporting both Pydantic V2 (BaseModel) and standard Python 3.10+ dataclasses, it automatically infers primitive types (str, int, float, bool), creates nested model classes, handles Optional fields and List typing, and generates Field(alias="...") definitions for non-Pythonic keys. jsonToPydantic.feature1: Dual Schema Generation: Seamlessly toggle between Pydantic V2 BaseModel syntax and native standard-library @dataclass
jsonToPydantic.feature2: Pythonic Naming & Aliasing: Converts camelCase keys to snake_case attributes with automated Pydantic Field(alias=...) support
jsonToPydantic.feature3: Type Hints & Optional Support: Generates modern PEP 484/604 type annotations including List[T] and Optional[T]
jsonToPydantic.feature4: Zero Server Exposure: Payload parsing and Python code generation run 100% locally in browser memory

jsonToPydantic.faq2Q: How does it handle JSON keys with dashes or reserved keywords?

fixMySpeaker.title: Fix My Speaker
fixMySpeaker.subtitle: Eject water and clear dust from your phone speakers using sound waves and vibration.
fixMySpeaker.soundDescription: Plays a high-frequency water-ejection sound wave designed to shake water droplets out of speaker grills.
fixMySpeaker.vibrateDescription: Uses low-frequency vibration pulses to dislodge trapped water droplets and dust particles.
fixMySpeaker.tip1: Turn your device volume all the way up to 100% for maximum acoustic ejection force.
fixMySpeaker.tip2: Hold or place your phone with the speaker facing downward so gravity assists water escape.
fixMySpeaker.tip3: Run 2 to 3 cycles if your speaker was heavily submerged or still sounds muffled.
fixMySpeaker.tip4: Gently wipe expelled water droplets away with an absorbent cloth or tissue.
fixMySpeaker.aboutText: Fix My Speaker is a free online audio utility that helps remove trapped water and dislodge dust from smartphone speakers, earbuds, and smartwatch audio grills. When a phone is dropped in water or exposed to moisture, water droplets can get stuck in the fine speaker mesh, muffling sound and potentially damaging internal components. By generating specifically tuned sound waves between 165 Hz and 250 Hz alongside vibration pulses, this tool creates strong acoustic air pressure that forces liquid droplets out through the speaker vents.
fixMySpeaker.feature1: Tuned 165Hz–250Hz acoustic sound waves for maximum liquid ejection force
fixMySpeaker.feature2: Dual-action cleaning with Sound and Haptic Vibration modes
fixMySpeaker.feature3: Fully client-side — works instantly in browser with no app download
fixMySpeaker.feature4: Safe for iPhone, Android, Apple Watch, iPad, and laptop speakers
fixMySpeaker.step1Body: Set your device volume to maximum level. The higher the volume, the stronger the sound vibrations will be to push water out.
fixMySpeaker.step2Body: Choose Sound Mode for acoustic air expulsion or Vibrate Mode for deep mechanical shaking. You can also alternate between both.
fixMySpeaker.step3Title: Click Play and keep phone facing down
fixMySpeaker.step3Body: Position your phone with the speaker holes facing downward so gravity helps eject the expelled water droplets, then press Play for the 30-second cycle.
fixMySpeaker.faq1Q: Will this damage my phone speaker?
fixMySpeaker.faq1A: No. The sound frequencies and volume levels used are completely within standard operating ranges for smartphone and mobile speakers. It will not blow out or harm your hardware when used normally.
fixMySpeaker.faq2Q: How long should I run the speaker cleaner?
fixMySpeaker.faq2A: A single cycle runs for 30 seconds. For mild moisture, 1 or 2 cycles are usually sufficient. If your phone was fully submerged in water, run 3 to 5 cycles until sound clarity is fully restored.
fixMySpeaker.faq3Q: Why is my speaker still muffled after running the tool?
fixMySpeaker.faq3A: If sound remains muffled, there may still be moisture deep inside the speaker chamber. Allow the phone to stand speaker-down in a dry, ventilated area for 15–30 minutes, then run Sound Mode again.
fixMySpeaker.faq4Q: Does this tool work on iPhone, Android, and other devices?
fixMySpeaker.faq4A: Yes! Fix My Speaker works across all modern web browsers on iPhone, Android phones, tablets, smartwatches, and laptops with zero installation.

imageCompressor.aboutText: Image Compressor is a modern, high-performance browser-based optimization tool designed to dramatically shrink JPEG, PNG, and WebP image sizes. By leveraging HTML5 Canvas rendering and native browser image compression codecs, your pictures are compressed entirely on your device with complete privacy. No images are ever sent over the network or saved to remote servers.
imageCompressor.feature1: 100% Client-Side Privacy: Images never leave your browser or device
imageCompressor.feature2: Flexible Compression Slider: Dial in the ideal balance of file weight and image clarity from 10% to 100%
imageCompressor.feature3: Multi-Format Converter: Seamlessly convert between JPEG, PNG, and next-gen WebP formats
imageCompressor.feature4: Batch Processing & ZIP Export: Compress multiple images simultaneously and download them in a single archive
imageCompressor.step1Body: Drag and drop one or multiple JPEG, PNG, or WebP images into the designated drop zone, or click to choose files from your computer or smartphone.
imageCompressor.step2Body: Adjust the compression slider (default 80%) and select your preferred output format (JPEG, PNG, or WebP) to tune file size and quality.
imageCompressor.step3Body: Inspect the before-and-after file sizes and percentage saved, then click Download for individual files or Download All (ZIP) to get all optimized photos.
imageCompressor.faq1Q: Are my images uploaded to any server?
imageCompressor.faq1A: No, absolutely not. All image decoding, canvas manipulation, and compression happens entirely within your web browser using client-side JavaScript. Your photos never leave your device.
imageCompressor.faq2Q: What compression quality should I choose?
imageCompressor.faq2A: For most photographic and web graphics, a quality setting between 75% and 85% is ideal. It typically reduces file weight by 60% to 80% while retaining crisp visual details indistinguishable from the original.
imageCompressor.faq3Q: Why is WebP recommended over JPEG or PNG?
imageCompressor.faq3A: WebP is a modern image format developed by Google that provides superior lossy and lossless compression. WebP images are generally 25%–35% smaller than comparable JPEGs and PNGs at equivalent visual quality.
imageCompressor.faq4Q: Is there a limit on how many images I can compress?
imageCompressor.faq4A: There are no server limits or paywalls. You can process dozens of images at once, bounded only by your browser's local memory and processor capability.

imageFormatConverter.faq1Q: Are my files uploaded or stored on any server?
imageFormatConverter.faq1A: No! All image conversions take place entirely within your browser using HTML5 Canvas. Your images never leave your local device.
imageFormatConverter.faq2Q: What happens to transparent backgrounds when converting PNG to JPEG?
imageFormatConverter.faq2A: Since the JPEG specification does not support an alpha transparency channel, transparent pixels are automatically rendered on a clean white background.
imageFormatConverter.faq3Q: Which image format should I convert to?
imageFormatConverter.faq3A: Choose WebP for the best combination of quality and small file size for the web. Choose PNG if you need transparent graphics or lossless icons. Choose JPEG for wide compatibility with older software and photography.
imageFormatConverter.faq4Q: Is there a limit on how many images I can convert at once?
